messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 - runtime node flutter in us-west-2 (inference-pool-14). Symptoms: repeated container crashes on paged-attention allocator; progressive KV cache fragmentation; OOMs and occasional CUDA driver reset. Autoscaler triggered.

maya: I'm on it. Gathering logs + checking perf metrics.

samir: Taking pager. Which customers hit?

maya: Quick check: 2 customer-facing clusters saw increased 5xxs starting ~00:20 UTC. Short spikes of latency and containers restarting.

dave: I see node-level dmesg with 'out of memory: kill process' and 'NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus' on node ip-10-2-5-11.

alice: Stack traces show paged allocator failing alloc at kv_cache::alloc_slab +0x2f8. Attn: maybe fragmentation + slow leak.

chandra: Can we quiesce new inference requests to this pool? Route to fallback region?

maya: Added routing override: route policy -> avoid pool-14, fallback to pool-21 in eu-west. Will monitor.

samir: For live mitigation: suggested steps: 1) drain affected nodes, 2) trigger kvcache compaction job, 3) bump eviction aggressiveness, 4) reschedule high-retention KV caches.

dave: How do we trigger compaction? I have a script but want to avoid heavy IO.

maya: Use internal tool: /run kvcache compact --pool inference-pool-14 --mode incremental. It does per-slot compaction.

alice: Command output from one node:
```
[2026-03-17T00:28:04Z] kvcache: slots=16384 used=15990 frag_ratio=0.78 evict_rate=0.002
[2026-03-17T00:28:05Z] paged-alloc: reclaims=12 pages freed=0
[2026-03-17T00:28:06Z] cuda: driver_reset_count=1
```
Shows high fragmentation, low reclaim.

samir: Run compaction with throttle and watch eviction metrics. If compaction stalls, we risk longer GC pauses.

maya: I'm running compaction now on node-11 (PID 4123). Visible logs:
```
compaction: slot_scan_progress=0.4
compaction: reclaimed_pages=120 out_of_cores=0
compaction: kv_evictions=450
```
No immediate crash after compaction started.

dave: Still seeing occasional 'CUDA_ERROR_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT' in containers that survived. Could be driver-sided resets from high reclaim.

chandra: Customer impact: two customers on pool-14 saw 5xx rate ~3.2% for 10min, some requests timed out. Support notified.

maya: Opened ticket CS-4521, included request IDs and sample stacktraces. CC'ing support.

alice: Plan for next hour: 1) finish compaction across nodes, 2) increase kv eviction aggressive factor from 0.002 -> 0.01 for pool-14, 3) spin up replacement nodes in us-west-2 pool-21

samir: Agree. Also suggest enabling 'fallback-variant' for models with high KV retention to lower memory footprint (quantized variants).

dave: I will cordon node-11 after compaction completes and drain pods. If node still flakes post-drain, we redeploy with nv-driver rollback.

maya: :thumbsup: compaction finished on node-11, reclaimed ~1.2GB. Node stable for 3m.

chandra: Support update: customers see error windows shrink, continuing monitoring.

alice: Postmortem note: We should add a watch that alerts when frag_ratio > 0.7 and reclaim_rate < 0.01 for >5m. That would catch slow creep.

samir: Also add a safe rolling compaction that runs during low RLQ load and doesn't block inference threads.

maya: I'm writing runbook updates now. Will add command snippets and escalation checklist.

dave: One node (ip-10-2-5-12) still threw NVRM reset after compaction; collected nvdiag logs and kernel oops. Marking for hardware investigation.

chandra: Customer communication: we informed impacted customers that mitigations applied, monitoring continues, follow-up planned.

maya: Switching handoff to night oncall @samir in 20m. Leaving summary: compaction reclaimed 3.8GB across pool; eviction bump in place; routing override active. Anything else?

samir: I have it. Will keep routing override for 30m and monitor metrics. If relapse, escalate to eng-runtime.

alice: Adding ticket for long-term: refactor paged allocator to reduce microfragmentation and add proactive compaction.

maya: :rotating_light: Incident status -> mitigated, but not resolved. ETA for full remediation TBD.
